Hi,

You could try this:

http://stackoverflow.com/questions/9538429/how-to-convert-r-expressions-to-latex-tex-without-using-a-cas

I'm not sure how general the translation to latex can be though.

HTH,

baptiste

On 15 March 2013 03:28, <niravm...@gmail.com> wrote:
I am writing to see whether the following functionality is available using R + knitr. 

I am using R to solve models numerically. I typically have functions such as 

ces<-function(elasticity, share1, share2) function(input1, input2)
{
(share1 * input1^(elasticity) + share2 * input2^(elasticity))^(1/elasticity)
}

that sometimes are easy to mistype. I was hoping that I could use knitr as a way of viewing these equations, without having to re-enter them using LaTeX. This would enable me to create the model section of my paper while coding the model for computation at the same time.

latex("(share1 * input1^(sigma) + share2 * input2^(sigma))^(1/sigma)", greek=TRUE)

but cannot figure out how to then transfer it to the non-R block part of the document. I may be missing something very simple.
